approval_required_for: Resolving ambiguous sample-project top, wrapper, block-design, clock/reset, AXI/DDR interface, or address-space choices when cited discovery evidence does not select a unique target.
Any architecture, multi-layer pipeline structure, memory layout, runtime ABI/register-map, or major trusted-template change required for closure.
Any numeric-policy or tolerance change other than applying the authorized frozen framework loose defaults when current-run tolerance values were initially absent.
Any modification to the exact user-supplied sample-wrapper sources or their immutable hashes; an approved change requires a new canonical simulation identity and complete board rerun.
Any repair that exceeds bounded wrapper glue, loader/harness, instrumentation, or runtime-programming scope.

executable_actions.on_failure: Classify absent or invalid checkpoint coverage, reference inference, tolerance, harness, or serialization evidence as a checker/golden-reference or loader capability failure. Do not generate expected values randomly or from RTL, do not accept sampled weights, and do not promote any hardware layer.
executable_actions.rationale: Board functional correctness needs complete Transformer-block weights and an independent target-model output for the same immutable checkpoint and stimulus. Random generation may create only the stimulus; expected outputs must be captured from the real target model before board simulation.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep case_multilayer_pipeline, wrapper generation, simulation, and backend blocked. If more than one interface target remains plausible, emit cited alternatives and request bounded approval; do not guess a top, wrapper, clock, reset, AXI port, DDR range, module, or path.
executable_actions.rationale: The exact wrapper, source set, top, clocks, resets, AXI/DDR configuration, project properties, and simulation identity must be derived from the current user-supplied sample project and cited real tool evidence rather than guessed from generic names.

executable_actions.on_failure: Reject unsupported wrapper assumptions and retain the exact sample-project sources unchanged. Route a pipeline-contract mismatch to the pipeline specialist and a memory/runtime mismatch to bounded memory/runtime repair. If closure requires a new memory layout, runtime ABI, architecture, or major wrapper template, stop for approval rather than substituting a simplified wrapper.
executable_actions.rationale: Bind trusted integration glue to the discovered exact sample wrapper and reconcile board memory, runtime, AXI transfer, and Stage 3 logical stream-order contracts before dynamic simulation.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not classify hardware correctness or proceed to Vivado. Preserve all immutable identity inputs, send the real simulator trace to the contract-guided localization action, and repair only the earliest proven causal implementation, loader, instrumentation, or integration boundary.
executable_actions.rationale: Execute the exact board wrapper and generated DUT with the immutable semantic inputs and complete Transformer-block DDR weight image. The resulting run manifest becomes the sole canonical identity consumed by all third-layer classifiers.

executable_actions.on_failure: Identify the earliest failing transaction and boundary before proposing code changes. Invoke contract-guided localization; preserve lower-layer certificates unless a contradictory bound trace justifies a targeted backtrack, and do not advance to DDR semantic aggregation or backend.
executable_actions.rationale: Derive multi-layer function, liveness, AXI handshake, address, burst, response, ordering, beat packing, and transfer-count results from the same canonical simulator execution rather than independent or static-only runs.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not alter expected output or tolerance. Localize whether the first mismatch is image generation, loader binding, AXI address/order, DUT consumption, output serialization, or DUT value generation; then repair that bounded cause and rerun the canonical board layer.
executable_actions.rationale: Prove bit-accurate input and weight serialization, complete required Transformer-block weight consumption, output address/count/order behavior, and numeric agreement of decoded output with independent target-model block-boundary values.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep case_vivado_synthesis and all later backend, bitstream, ABI, and board-runtime actions blocked. Return the failed or missing subgate and canonical identity to its owner; do not rewrite checker results, loosen tolerance, or aggregate a partial pass.
executable_actions.rationale: Create one checker-bound board promotion certificate that joins current-valid lower-layer certificates, exact wrapper identity, canonical simulation identity, dynamic classifiers, complete weight consumption, and target-model numeric comparison. Backend may consume only this aggregate, never isolated subgate logs.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the failed layer and all higher layers blocked. Do not patch a downstream symptom. If localization cannot distinguish multiple roots, request bounded diagnostic approval or additional instrumentation rather than guessing a module.
produces: conditional stage backtrack request with contradictory trace evidence
executable_actions.rationale: Every real-tool liveness, value, order, or protocol failure must be reduced to the earliest causal boundary before repair. A lower-layer backtrack is allowed only when the board trace contradicts its current certificate.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep promotion blocked and return to localization. If repair requires architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, runtime-ABI, numeric-policy, tolerance, major-template, or exact sample-wrapper source changes, stop and request approval; any approved identity-changing change must start a new canonical run rather than reuse prior evidence.
produces: updated failed-gate evidence under the same immutable contract
executable_actions.rationale: Repair only the implementation, bounded wrapper glue, loader/harness, runtime programming, or instrumentation identified by the causal repair context while preserving checkpoint, stimulus, reference output, tolerance, semantic testbench, memory layout, and exact wrapper hashes.

observations: The visible Stage 6 verification artifact contract reports pass, upstream Stage 3 through Stage 5 static gates are visible, and the declared hierarchy enforces operator-leaf closure before single-layer closure and single-layer closure before board AXI/DDR closure.
sacg_memory_truth reports zero active contamination barriers and zero open retry or backtrack requests. Historical records therefore create no current blocker.

The role slice reports 36 DAG nodes, 27 evidence gates, 36 evidence-path requirements, and complete stage-agent coverage. Detailed rows omitted by the role slice are treated as present because the static contract checker passed; the aggregate auditor should use the unsliced artifact rather than infer missing rows here.

The generated AXI/DDR top compiled and elaborated, but that evidence proves only structural generation. It does not prove that the generated integration uses the exact user-supplied sample-project wrapper, source set, top, clocks, resets, AXI port configuration, DDR model, simulation options, or source hashes.

The exact sample-project wrapper must be discovered from artifact.input.sample_project_index, target-board evidence, and real project-tool evidence. A simplified wrapper or framework-core hardcoding of the case-specific model, board, module, or path is prohibited.

The current certificate-validation summary marks operator-leaf, single-layer, and board AXI/DDR promotion certificates missing or stale for the current contract. These are downstream execution obligations rather than failures of the ready Stage 6 static contract. Board execution must wait for a current-valid single-layer certificate.

The board wrapper gate also consumes case_multilayer_pipeline evidence. Generation and semantic closure of that pipeline belong to the corresponding pipeline specialist; this role will reject an AXI/DDR handoff that lacks its current checker-bound certificate.

The upstream parameter binding records clock_target_mhz as 0. Board discovery must bind the actual clock/reset facts from the exact sample project or report ambiguity; it must not guess a frequency from a generic board template.

The address/order contract must reconcile memory-layout bases, extents, alignment, non-overlap, transfer counts, AXI beat bytes, byte-lane and endianness mapping, burst boundaries, ID/order behavior, logical token/channel/tile/lane order, runtime register values, and the declared 16/32-bit cast boundaries.

A checkpoint manifest or DDR weight image is not consumption proof. The board certificate requires complete Transformer-block tensor hashes, a hashed loader/harness binding each required tensor to DDR ranges, and executed transaction or DUT instrumentation showing every required range was consumed.

The board golden boundary is the output of all accelerated Transformer blocks. Embedding and tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, sampling, and other model-tail operations remain outside DUT implementation, weight coverage, DDR acceptance scope, and expected-output comparison.

The canonical board simulation identity must bind checkpoint catalog, deterministic or real stimulus, target-model reference outputs, frozen numeric policy and tolerance, semantic testbench, lower-layer certificates, memory layout, runtime configuration, exact sample-wrapper source set, generated DUT and glue sources, DDR images, loader/harness, compile/elaboration commands, simulator version, and executed simulation outputs.
proposed_actions: Prepare and hash the complete Transformer-block checkpoint catalog, immutable stimulus, target-model block-boundary outputs, resolved frozen tolerance, semantic testbench, and bound loader requirements.

After a current-valid single-layer certificate exists, execute exact sample-project interface discovery and emit a cited target_discovery_policy plus wrapper/source identity; stop for bounded approval if project evidence is ambiguous.
Receive a checker-valid case_multilayer_pipeline certificate from the pipeline specialist before binding the AXI/DDR wrapper.
Generate only bounded integration glue around the exact discovered sample wrapper, then statically reconcile the address map, runtime ABI, transfer units, burst policy, and logical data order.
Run the canonical board-wrapped real simulator and retain complete transaction, liveness, boundary, weight-access, and DDR image evidence under one immutable identity.
Classify multi-layer functionality, deadlock/liveness, AXI protocol/address/order behavior, and DDR input/weight/output roundtrip from that same run.

Aggregate all current-valid lower-layer and third-layer evidence into artifact.stage7.board_axi_ddr_promotion_certificate; hand the certificate and strict backend boundary to verification_artifacts.cross_layer_evidence_gate_auditor.
For any failure, localize the earliest violated boundary before repair, preserve immutable semantic inputs, and rerun the failed layer before any higher-layer or backend action.
risks: Backend promotion remains blocked until a current-contract board AXI/DDR promotion certificate exists; this is a required later-stage gate, not a current Stage 6 static-contract failure.

If board discovery finds multiple plausible tops, wrappers, block designs, clocks, resets, AXI interfaces, or DDR address spaces, selecting one without cited evidence would contaminate every later board and backend result.
The zero clock target can cause clock/reset or runtime mismatch if generic defaults are substituted instead of binding the exact sample-project facts.

Static address-map and stream-order availability cannot establish dynamic protocol correctness. Burst crossing, beat packing, response handling, backpressure, ordering, transfer-count, or liveness faults may only appear in the canonical board-wrapped simulation.

A bit-correct DDR image roundtrip can still be insufficient if the DUT did not read every required Transformer-block weight. Complete access coverage must be joined with tensor-to-range hashes and loader/harness identity.

Changing checkpoint, stimulus, target-model outputs, tolerance, testbench, memory layout, runtime ABI, or exact wrapper source hashes during repair would invalidate comparison evidence and require a new canonical run identity.

A third-layer failure may expose a contradictory lower-layer boundary trace. Such evidence must trigger a targeted backtrack to the earliest causal layer; it must not be patched only in the board wrapper or used to skip the operator and single-layer repair order.
Adding embedding, final norm, LM head, logits, or sampling data to the board golden or complete-weight requirement would create a scope mismatch with the Transformer-block-only accelerator contract.

edges: case_semantic_testbench + case_single_layer_semantic_evidence + case_multilayer_pipeline + case_board_interface_discovery + case_axi_ddr_interface -> functional_sim
all third-layer classifiers + immutable semantic inputs -> case_board_semantic_evidence

output.summary: The Stage 6 verification contract is statically ready and the third-layer ordering is sound: current-contract single-layer closure, exact sample-project interface discovery, peer-produced multi-layer pipeline closure, exact AXI/DDR wrapper binding, canonical board-wrapped simulation, dynamic protocol and DDR roundtrip classification, then board semantic aggregation. No current SACG-memory blocker is listed. No board functional pass or backend promotion is claimed: all three promotion certificates are absent or invalid for the current contract, and the board certificate must be produced from executed real-tool evidence before Vivado synthesis is permitted.
